OAT-06/S25.title: Native app on the local stack: events fire from the app; a wrong-date device files them on the server's day
OAT-06/S25.detail: Android rig: debug build of main e02167f bundled for the LOCAL stack only (bundle names 127.0.0.1:4510/4511, reached through adb reverse), built outside the checkout, on the rc_api36 emulator (Pixel 7, Android 16); Playwright attached to the app's own WebView; every ai/* action the app sends is answered or failed at the WebView's socket (no model call; aiCallLog had no new row in any run). Our addition (10-15 review): recorded only. On the Android app with the phone one day behind in Pacific/Honolulu: open a chart, complete a task, delete a task, Mark Encounter Complete; the same on the desktop for another patient. Admin reads on the local backend: the app fires the same four events as the desktop (pre_round_summary_opened, task_completed, task_deleted, note_marked_complete), but every phone row carries day 2026-10-13 (the phone's day) and lands in a separate pilotDailyRounding row, while the desktop's are 2026-10-15 - the device-day behaviour the code read predicted (usage day = localDay()). Not run: sending a handoff (needs a colleague account) and the handoff follow-up survey. iOS half not run: the simulator cannot be tapped here without a permission prompt (no idb / Maestro / WebDriverAgent installed; the simulator-control and computer-use tools ask first), and the only booted simulator runs someone else's dev-pointed build (b8fb762), which was left alone. A separate prompt-free smoke on a new simulator (dvc-tc24-s24-ios-*) showed the iOS build on the local stack opening and listing patients.
